Jordan P.: FYI rack-7 hit sustained p99 GPU latency + host pci backlog at 03:12 UTC. Small chat tenants spiked. Likely noisy neighbor doing large synchronous copies.
Rina H.: saw the same. `ethtool -S` and `nvidia-smi dmon` show persistent tx bytes + mem bw for tenant `img-batch`. NVLINK counters high.
Sam C.: short-term mitigation: migrate img-batch to reserved-warm-1 to relieve rack. Will cost cache rebuild but buys room.
Vikram D.: long-term options: 1) per-tenant NIC egress shaping (token bucket via eBPF), 2) fractional GPU slices (25/50%) as billed SKU, 3) scheduler-level soft-isolation (move heavy pods proactively).
Jordan P.: can we avoid whole-pod moves often? customers hate cache loss. Prefer shaping + soft-isolation.
Rina H.: created branch `egress-limit/ebpf-token` that maps tenant IP->cgroup throttle. Tests show small RPCs (<2KB) unaffected with burst=5MB and rate=200Mbps.
Sam C.: product needs pricing for fractional slices. If we offer 25% reserved slice at ~40% of full GPU cost, we could monetize heavy tenants and reduce incidents.
Vikram D.: risk of shaping: incorrectly tuned caps may increase tail. We'll canary in us-central for 15m. Deploy command: `deploy-bot deploy egress-limit/ebpf-token --target=us-central-rackpool-2 --ttl=15m`.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled.
ops-bot: INC-2026-044 opened for rack-7 noisy neighbor. Owner: Rina H.
Rina H.: manual migration executed: `kubectl drain gpu-07-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> router weight update. Monitoring shows p95 for affected tenants returning to baseline.
Jordan P.: next actions: 1) telemetry rule to detect NVLINK/DMA flurries and trigger soft-shield (Rina), 2) roll eBPF canary and evaluate tail effects (Vikram), 3) pricing ticket for 25%/50% fractional SKU (Sam).
Sam C.: filing pricing ticket and quick UX mock for Console "soft-carveout" flow.
Vikram D.: starting canary now. Will report metrics after 10m.
Rina H.: leaving INC open until fractional SKU decision. Eventual goal: prefer shaping + opt-in reserved slices over disruptive live-migrations. :thumbsup:
